The summary endpoint is feature-flagged off in the local stack and the test tenants have no XPM rows, so the agent can only partially execute end-to-end. Once the flag flips and a client connects XPM, the core path works.

sections.section: Chart of accounts mapping to HMRC SA103/SA105 categories
sections.note: Verified 91 accounts returned for 11668 - agent could pattern-match account names to HMRC SA103 categories (Travel, Rent, etc.) but there is NO existing mapping table, taxonomy, or system field linking COA accounts to HMRC categories. Agent would have to hand-classify.
No MTD readiness service; would need new endpoint that scores accounts against HMRC taxonomy.
Total revenue from P&L works, but threshold logic is for qualifying income (self-employment + property only, NOT PAYE/dividends/pensions) - and no tool separates those streams.
Tracking categories surface exists but is not specifically set up for MTD income-class separation.

sections.section: Finance cost separation (residential vs commercial mortgage)
sections.note: No mortgage-classification capability.
Total turnover from P&L gives the 90k cutoff, but eligibility also depends on income type.

rationale: MTD-ITSA is structurally different from VAT/BAS/GST/IAS - it needs an HMRC SA103/SA105 category mapping that XBert does not yet expose as a first-class concept. Agent could produce a hand-wavy 'looks ready / looks not ready' answer purely from COA pattern matching, but core capability for an actual readiness assessment is missing.
